title: A plate cooling from both faces
statement: A plate $40\ \text{mm}$ thick is at $200\ ^\circ\text{C}$ throughout when both its faces are suddenly held at $20\ ^\circ\text{C}$. Its diffusivity is $\alpha = 12\ \text{mm}^2/\text{s}$. Find the temperatures across it after $t = 30\ \text{s}$.

artefact.caption: The plate at $t = 30\ \text{s}$, face to face

steps.title: Read the problem
steps.note: The plate cools from both faces alike, so it stays symmetric about its mid-plane, $x = 20\ \text{mm}$. Work in $\theta = \frac{T - T_s}{T_i - T_s}$, which falls from $1$ towards $0$.

steps.title: The faces
steps.note: Both faces are held at $T_s$ from the start: $T = 20.0\ ^\circ\text{C}$ at $x = 0$ and at $x = 40\ \text{mm}$.

steps.title: Fourier number
steps.note: $\mathrm{Fo} = \frac{\alpha t}{L^2} = \frac{12 \times 30}{40^2} = 0.225$. Past $0.2$ the series' first term is enough: $\theta = \frac{4}{\pi} \sin\left(\frac{\pi x}{L}\right) e^{-\pi^2 \mathrm{Fo}}$.

steps.title: The mid-plane
steps.note: At $x = 20\ \text{mm}$ the sine is $1$: $\theta = \frac{4}{\pi} e^{-2.2207} = 0.1382$, so $T = 20 + 180 \times 0.1382 = 44.9\ ^\circ\text{C}$.

steps.title: The quarter points
steps.note: At $x = 10$ and $30\ \text{mm}$ the sine is $0.7071$: $\theta = 0.0977$, so $T = 20 + 180 \times 0.0977 = 37.6\ ^\circ\text{C}$.

answer: $T = 20.0$, $37.6$, $44.9$, $37.6$ and $20.0\ ^\circ\text{C}$ at $x = 0$, $10$, $20$, $30$ and $40\ \text{mm}$: after $30\ \text{s}$ the mid-plane is still $24.9\ ^\circ\text{C}$ above the faces

stated: the one-term series past $\mathrm{Fo} = 0.2$, with its $\frac{4}{\pi}$
